header.running_head: Hadhrat Ja'far bin Abi Taalib (RA) and Other Sahabah (RA) Migrate to Abyssinia and then to Madinah

Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) says, "We left and when we reached Madinah, Rasulullaah ﷺ met me and hugged me. He then said, 'I do not know whether I am happier without conquest at Khaybar or with the arrival of Ja'far." The arrival of Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) coincided with the Muslims' victory at Khaybar. When Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down, Najaashi's envoy said, "Ask Ja'far how our leader treated him." Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) said, "Why of course!" He then explained the excellent treatment that Najaashi gave them and that he had even provided transport and provisions for their journey. Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) also said, "Najaashi has testified that there is none worthy of worship but Allaah and that you are Allaah's Rasul. He also told me to ask you to seek forgiveness on his behalf." Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up, made wudhu and then said thrice, "O Allaah! Forgive Najaashi." All the Muslims said "Aameen" to this du'aa.
Hadhrat Ja'far (RA) then said to the envoy, "Go and tell your leader what you have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ do." [^1]
The Virtues of those Sahabah (RA) who Migrated to Abyssinia and then to Madinah

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ummu Abdillaah bint Abi Hathma (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Ummu Abdillaah bint Abi Hathma (RA) says, "By Allaah! We were preparing to leave for Abyssinia when (my husband) Aamir had to leave for something we needed. In the meantime, Hadhrat Umar (RA) who was still a Mushrik came to me. We had been suffering difficulties and cruel treatment at his hand. He said, 'O Ummu Abdillaah! Are you leaving?' 'We certainly are!' I replied, 'By Allaah! We are going to a land from the lands of Allaah because you people have harassed us and acted cruelly towards us until Allaah has made an escape for us.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, 'May Allaah go with you.' I saw such gentleness in him that I had never seen before. He then left and he seemed to be truly grieved by our departure. When Hadhrat Aamir returned after fulfilling the task, I said to him, 'O Abu Abdillaah! If only you had seen Umar just now. He was extremely gentle and actually grieved by our departure.' He asked, 'Are you hopeful that he will accept Islaam?' 'I certainly do,' I replied. Because Hadhrat Aamir had lost hope of Hadhrat Umar (RA) accepting Islaam after seeing his harshness and opposition against Islaam, he commented, 'The man you saw (Hadhrat Umar (RA)) shall never accept Islaam until the donkey of Khattaab accepts Islaam!'" [^2] The name of Hadhrat Ummu Abdillaah (RA) was Layla. [^3]
